statement: The literal functor of scan 23 sends a smooth projective anabelian $K$-scheme of dimension at most one to $\Pi_1(X)\longrightarrow\Pi_1(K)$. Its pointed version has morphisms $(f,\gamma):(X',\xi')\to(X,\xi)$, where $f$ is a $K$-morphism and $\gamma$ is an \'etale path from $f(\xi')$ to $\xi$. The path supplies the actual homomorphism of based groups. Passing to paths modulo target geometric conjugacy recovers the unpointed groupoid formulation. For a pair $(X,S)$ the boundary enhancement of scans 28--35 is the following diagram of profinite groupoids, with its displayed commutation isomorphism and its Kummer isomorphism: \[ \Pi_{D^*}\xrightarrow{\rho}\Pi_U\xrightarrow{\varphi}\Pi_e, \qquad \Pi_{D^*}\xrightarrow{\sigma}\Pi_D\xrightarrow{\psi}\Pi_e, \qquad \alpha:\varphi\rho\simeq\psi\sigma, \qquad \ker(\sigma)\simeq\psi^*T . \] Here $D_s=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,s}$, $D_s^*=D_s\setminus\{s\}$, $D=\coprod_{s\in S}D_s$ and $D^*=\coprod_{s\in S}D_s^*$. The map $\sigma$ induces a bijection on components and surjections on automorphism groups, its kernel is abelian, $\psi$ is faithful, and $\rho$ is faithful for hyperbolic curves. The images in $\Pi_e$ are open. After choosing one object in each component, the same data are $p:E\to\Gamma$, its kernel $\pi$, a finite index set $I$, injections $\rho_i:E_i\hookrightarrow E$, open images $\Gamma_i=p(E_i)$, and equivariant isomorphisms $k_i:T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i=E_i\cap\pi$. The image of $p$ is permitted to be open rather than all of $\Gamma$. Disjoint unions and the separate constant fields recover the non-geometrically-connected version.

statement: The computation above settles the abelian and metabelian failures, and the full and pro-prime equalities have been proved. The smallest $m\geq3$ with same-level commutant $S_3$ is not determined here. A theorem reconstructing the isomorphism class of a curve from its $m$-step quotient is insufficient: it supplies a map from isomorphism classes, whereas the required assertion concerns every element of an automorphism group. The precise additional map in Mochizuki's Theorem A$'$ forgets three derived steps. Yamaguchi's strong finite-step statements likewise specify the image in a lower-step quotient \cite{A_Yamaguchi2024}; they do not assert that the kernel of this forgetting map is trivial. The involutions just constructed make this distinction visible by an actual element and its images. The remaining task is to control that kernel or produce an arithmetic-centralizing lift through the next derived quotient. Proposition~\ref{A:solvable-projection-limit} below determines the exact lower-step images and the prosolvable limit; it does not determine this same-level kernel. Theorem~\ref{A:third-derived-IA} below eliminates the entire IA image from length three to two, and Corollary~\ref{A:third-derived-projection} identifies the whole projected peripheral commutant with the geometric $S_3$. Thus the remaining same-level question is the kernel of the third-to-second-derived map, not the lifting of the metabelian unit family.

statement: For the full CM group the remaining problem is the existence or exclusion of a nontrivial closed procyclic $C\subset R$ whose normalizer in the arithmetic full profinite group has open image in $G_{\mathbf Q(i)}$. Proposition~\ref{A:deeper-common-kernel} below further forces any such $C$ into the strictly smaller group $R_{\rm nil}(F')\subset F''$. No such subgroup has been constructed or excluded here. For a general affine hyperbolic curve the same bare-normalizer problem also remains unresolved here. It is not settled by the primewise theorem or by the cyclotomic-kernel centralizer theorem. The additional restrictions in Propositions~\ref{A:full-support-normalizer} and \ref{A:cm-normalizer-field} below settle cofinite prime support and all normalizer fields containing no CM subfield. Over an imaginary quadratic normalizer field the residual support can contain only split primes. These restrictions apply to the actual full profinite subgroup in this remark. The actual attacks and their exact stopping points are as follows. Lower central quotients and all maximal pro-prime quotients leave precisely $R$. Passing to a finite cover detects every nonidentity element in homology, but its line can have weight one; the proof does not make that character cyclotomic. For a CM detecting factor the restriction to $G_{K^{\rm ab}}$ is trivial, so replacing $K(\mu_\infty)$ by $K^{\rm ab}$ invalidates the no-torus-to-abelian-variety hypothesis: both $T_\ell E_0$ and $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$ become trivial. The Prym refinement has also been checked directly. For $Y\to U$ finite \'etale, an element in $R$ has proper homology in $\ker(V_\ell J_{\overline Y}\to V_\ell E_0)$. In genus one this kernel is zero, so a weight-one residual detector requires genus at least two. Sending its Jacobian factor to an elliptic curve does not automatically give a punctured map. A map $f:\overline Y\to E'$ restricts to $Y\to E'\setminus\{q\}$ precisely when $\operatorname{Supp}f^{-1}(q)$ lies in the existing boundary. Riemann--Hurwitz then forces $\deg f\leq\deg(Y/U)$. The concrete map $[3]:E_0\to E_0$ on the cover $E_0\setminus E_0[2]\to U$ still surjects onto all of $E_0$, although it detects proper Tate homology. Thus it supplies no such punctured map. Adding punctures requires an arithmetic-equivariant lift; the class-five obstruction above is an explicit case in which that lift fails. A further approach using a normalizer extension as a source for the Hom theorem stops at the same precise issue: it is an infinite-index arithmetic subgroup, not the fundamental group of a finite-type source for which the required open Hom theorem applies. Its projection onto an open Galois group supplies no section by itself. The finite metabelian example above confirms, by an actual mixed-prime element, why primewise tests leave additional information. It is not a counterexample inside $\pi$ to the normalizer assertion. A genuinely new argument on the residual Prym part or a compatible full profinite construction is still required.

statement: Let $U/k$ be hyperbolic over a number field, $x\in U(k)$, and $\iota:k\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$. Every extension $j:\bar k\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ gives a dense discrete subgroup \[ \Lambda_j=\operatorname{im}\bigl( \pi_1^{\rm top}(U_\iota(\mathbb C),x_\iota) \longrightarrow\Delta_U\bigr) \] whose profinite completion is $\Delta_U$. Use $x$ for the effective action $\rho_x:G_k\to\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta_U)$, and let $\sigma\cdot j=j\circ\sigma^{-1}$. Then \[ \Lambda_{\sigma\cdot j}=\rho_x(\sigma)(\Lambda_j),\qquad \operatorname{Stab}_{G_k}(\Lambda_j)=G_{v,j}. \] Here $G_{v,j}=1$ at a complex place and is the order-two group of complex conjugation at a real place. The stabilizer of the oriented lattice is $1$. The unoriented orbit is $G_k/G_{v,j}$ and the oriented orbit is a free transitive $G_k$-set of these comparisons. Thus the effective action does not make the discretization independent of the embedding choice.

statement: Fix a hyperbolic type $(g,n)$, its geometric full profinite curve group $\Delta$, and its prescribed peripheral conjugacy classes. For each nonempty stable multicurve type, choose oriented generators $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in\Delta$ of its node groups. Call their $A$-translates, with arbitrary individual conjugations, \emph{pro-simple multicurve tuples}. Let $k$ be a number field, let $E\twoheadrightarrow G_k$ be a profinite extension, and let $\rho:E\to\operatorname{Out}(\Delta)$ be continuous, with the image of the geometric kernel contained in $Q$. The following condition on a continuous section $s$ defines a closed, geometric-conjugacy-invariant subset of its section space: there is a nonempty pro-simple multicurve tuple such that, for every $\gamma\in G_k$, there are a permutation $\sigma$ and signs $\epsilon_i\in\{1,-1\}$ satisfying \[ \rho(s(\gamma))(c_i) \ \sim_\Delta\quad c_{\sigma(i)}^{\epsilon_i\chi(\gamma)} \qquad(1\leq i\leq r). \tag{B.36.1} \] Here the left side is a conjugacy class, so the condition is independent of the representative of the outer automorphism. No outer action satisfying this condition is the peripheral outer action of a smooth marked curve over $k$, or over any finite extension of $k$ after restriction.

statement: Let $k$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, choose $q\in k$ with $0<|q|<1$, and let $E_q/k$ be the Tate elliptic curve. Put $B=E_q\setminus\{O\}$. statement: Fix an orientation-reversing mapping class $\sigma$ of a compact genus-$g$ surface, $g\geq2$, with $r$ real ovals. Retain $E_+$, $\ell$ and any primitive cocycle $h$ of E.13. For every rational prime $p
e2,\ell$, choose an arithmetic Frobenius and define \[ u_p=(F_{E,p}-1)^{-1}h(F_p),\qquad \operatorname{ord}(u_p+V)=\ell^{m_p},\quad m_p\ge0. 	ag{E14.1} \] This is the local cohomology class under the explicit isomorphism \[ V/(F_{E,p}-1)V\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\  igl((V\otimes\mathbb Q_\ell)/V igr)^{F_{E,p}}, \qquad [x]\longmapsto(F_{E,p}-1)^{-1}x+V. 	ag{E14.2} \] The integer $m_p$ is independent of the Frobenius prolongation, the cocycle representative, the integral Tate basis, and multiplication of $[h]$ by a unit. For $q>1$ and $n\ge1$ put \[ T_q(n)= rac{q^{2-n}}{q^2-1}. \] The following are natural densities relative to the indicated set of rational primes; all of them exist: \[  egin{array}{c|cc} &p\equiv1\pmod4&p\equiv3\pmod4\\hline \ell=3:\ m_p\ge n&T_9(n)&T_3(n)\ \ell=5:\ m_p\ge n&2T_5(n)-T_5(n)^2&T_5(n). \end{array} 	ag{E14.3} \] In particular, among all rational primes, the exact tails are \[  egin{split} \delta_3(m_p\ge n)&= rac{9^{2-n}}{160} + rac{3^{2-n}}{16},\ \delta_5(m_p\ge n)&= rac{5^{2-n}}{16} - rac{5^{4-2n}}{1152}. \end{split} 	ag{E14.4} \] The masses at zero and at every positive integer are \[  egin{array}{c|cc} &\delta(m_p=0)&\delta(m_p=n),\quad n\ge1\\hline \ell=3&121/160&9^{1-n}/20+3^{1-n}/8\ \ell=5&817/1152&5^{1-n}/4-5^{2-2n}/48. \end{array} 	ag{E14.5} \] Each positive exponent has positive density. For a nonzero scalar $r\in\mathbb Z_\ell$, with $t=
u_\ell(r)$, the local exponents of $r[h]$ are exactly $\max(m_p-t,0)$; their positive tails are obtained by replacing $n$ with $n+t$ in (E14.3)--(E14.4). For a compact vector $(r_1[h],r_2[h],r_3[h])$, the analogous exponent is $\max(m_p-\min_i
u_\ell(r_i),0)$, with value zero when every $r_i$ is zero. These assertions apply to the primitive class used in the prior E.115 and E.117 and do not require the prior rank-one cohomology calculation.

statement: Let $\ell$ be odd, let $N$ be a free pro-$\ell$ group of finite rank with a specified continuous action of a profinite group $G$, and put $A=N^{\mathrm{ab}}$, $B=\bigwedge^2 A$. A choice of free lifts of a basis of $A$ gives the integral class-two coordinates \[ N/\gamma_3N=A\times B,\qquad (v,m)(w,n)=(v+w,m+n+\tfrac12v\wedge w). \tag{E15.1} \] Write the genuine arithmetic action as \[ g(v,m)=(A_gv,\ B_gm+D_gv),\qquad B_g=\bigwedge^2 A_g. \] For continuous one-cocycles $a,b:G\to A$, the obstruction to lifting $a$ through the actual class-two extension is represented by \[ \omega_a(g,h)=D_g a(h)+\tfrac12a(g)\wedge A_g a(h). \tag{E15.2} \] Its exact polarization is \[ \operatorname{ob}(a+b)-\operatorname{ob}(a) -\operatorname{ob}(b)=[a\cup_{\wedge}b] \quad\text{in }H^2_{\rm cts}(G,B). \tag{E15.3} \] Thus the sum of two liftable classes is liftable precisely on the zero locus of their displayed cup pairing. For the actual quartic decomposition of E.17, $A=W\oplus j(V^3)$ at $\ell=3,5$, where $V=T_\ell E_+$, the mixed component for $a=b+j_{\mathbf r}h$ has at every good prime $p\ne2,\ell$ the following actual local representative. Let $v_p=b(t_p)$ and $u_p=(F_{E,p}-1)^{-1}h(F_p)$, with the choices of E.14. Its unique rational tame correction is \[ c_p=v_p\wedge j_{\mathbf r}u_p . \tag{E15.4} \] Writing $t=\min_i v_\ell(r_i)$ and $\operatorname{ord}(u_p+V)=\ell^{m_p}$, this correction is integral exactly when \[ v_\ell(v_p)+t\ge m_p\qquad(m_p>0). \tag{E15.5} \] After replacing $u_p$ by its fractional representative, the sequence of corrections is restricted exactly when $v_\ell(v_p)+t-m_p\to+\infty$ on the primes with $m_p>0$. These are the polarization and mixed support maps in LM7 E.115 and E.117, with the arithmetic linear term retained. The density of the local inequality's failure at a fixed finite threshold $d=v_\ell(v_p)+t$ is the tail $\delta_\ell(m_p\ge d+1)$ of E.14; this statement concerns the local mixed test with that fixed threshold.

statement: Let $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, $r\ge1$, and $n=\ell^r$. Use the rational unit tangent at $[0:-1:1]\in X_n$ and the resulting genuine action on \[ N_n=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline{\mathbb Q}})^{(\ell)},\qquad V_n=N_n^{\rm ab},\qquad S=\{\ell,\infty\}. \] Every class of $H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S},V_n)$ lifts to a section of the full geometrically pro-$\ell$ arithmetic extension of $U_n/\mathbb Q$. There are infinitely many such classes whose lifts are cuspidal at no boundary point. Each retains this property in every positive-class intrinsic nilpotent quotient and every positive-length solvable quotient, through the compactified Jacobian quotient specified below. Here the cuspidal classes in a quotient are the images of the actual cusp packets under the displayed arithmetic quotient map. Thus no intrinsic pro-$3$ nilpotent level for $n=3^r$, and no intrinsic pro-$5$ nilpotent level for $n=5^r$, selects only cuspidal sections. This extends the checked mechanism of LM7 E.34 from the cubic to these two entire towers. It gives a specific range of the full section problem; the passage to all coefficient primes and mixed finite quotients is retained in E.21.

statement: Let $N=\pi_1(U_{3,\overline{\mathbb Q}})^{(3)}$, with the genuine action defined by the rational unit tangent at $O=[1:-1:0]$. Put $N_i=N/\gamma_{i+1}N$, $V=N^{\rm ab}$, $A=\gamma_3N/\gamma_4N=\operatorname{Lie}_3V$, and $K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)$. The rank of $A$ is $330$. Fix a continuous ordered-Hall set section $h:N_2\to N_3$ carrying one to one. For an actual continuous cocycle $a:G_{\mathbb Q}\to N_2$ and every prime $\mathfrak q\nmid3$ of $K$, choose a prolongation, positive tame generator $t_{\mathfrak q}$ and arithmetic Frobenius $F_{\mathfrak q}$. Write $q=N\mathfrak q$ and \[ \begin{aligned} n_{\mathfrak q}&=h(a(t_{\mathfrak q})),& x_{\mathfrak q}&=h(a(F_{\mathfrak q})),\\ \epsilon_{\mathfrak q} &=x_{\mathfrak q}\rho_3(F_{\mathfrak q})(n_{\mathfrak q}) x_{\mathfrak q}^{-1}n_{\mathfrak q}^{-q}\in A,& z_{\mathfrak q} &=-(\Phi_{\mathfrak q}-q)^{-1}\epsilon_{\mathfrak q} \in A\otimes\mathbb Q_3 . \end{aligned} \tag{E18.1} \] Here $\rho_3$ is the actual action on $N_3$ and $\Phi_{\mathfrak q}$ its induced action on $A$. The fibre over $[a]$ of \[ H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},N_3) \longrightarrow H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},N_2) \tag{E18.2} \] is nonempty precisely when every $z_{\mathfrak q}$ is integral and $z_{\mathfrak q}\to0$ in the uniform $3$-adic congruence topology. Each nonempty fibre is a torsor under the explicitly evaluated group \[ \mathbb Z_3^{166}\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)^7 \oplus(\mathbb Z/9)^{56}\oplus(\mathbb Z/27)^{25} \oplus(\mathbb Z/81)^3 . \tag{E18.3} \] For every class unramified outside $3$, this fibre is nonempty. At the $K$-prime $(2)$ the integral local obstruction module is \[ \coker(\Phi_{(2)}-4)= (\mathbb Z/3)^{70}\oplus(\mathbb Z/9)^{24} \oplus(\mathbb Z/27)^{76}\oplus(\mathbb Z/81)^{28}. \tag{E18.4} \] The test (E18.1) retains the higher action and the actual Frobenius cocycle values as data. Its proof and the two computed coefficient groups verify LM7 E.41 and E.44 in the degree used here. E.21 records the unevaluated arithmetic data for unrestricted inputs rather than counting this test as their complete evaluation.

Its class-three obstruction is the linear connecting homomorphism for the actual $G_{\mathbb Q}$-module sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow L \longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0 . \tag{E19.1} \] This whole obstruction is determined by the action on $N_2$. An action on $N_3$ need not be supplied separately for this slice. More precisely let $w=(3f_1+U_1)\wedge(3f_2+U_2)\in M$, in the integral coordinates (E18.9). It is primitive and spans a $G_{\mathbb Q}$-submodule $\mathbb Z_3(1)$. Every $[z]\in H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},M)$ has a unique decomposition \[ [z]=[z_0]+\beta w,\qquad [z_0]\in H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M), \qquad \beta=\sum_{p\ne3}a_p\kappa_3(p), \quad a_p\in\mathbb Z_3,\quad a_p\to0. \tag{E19.2} \] Choose a lift $\omega\in L$ of $w$ with $c\omega=-\omega$ for complex conjugation $c$. The actual continuous cocycle \[ \eta(g)=\chi(g)^{-1}\bigl(g\omega-\chi(g)\omega\bigr) \in A(-1) \tag{E19.3} \] is unramified outside three. The obstruction of (E19.2) is exactly \[ [\eta\cup\beta]\in H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},A). \tag{E19.4} \] Over $K$, its unique rational tame corrections are \[ -a_p\,(q^{-1}\Phi_{\mathfrak q}-1)^{-1} \eta(F_{\mathfrak q}), \qquad \mathfrak q\mid p,\quad p\ne3. \tag{E19.5} \] Thus the exact image in this slice is the kernel of the linear map (E19.4), equivalently the integral restricted locus of (E19.5); its nonempty fibres are (E18.3). The remaining action class (E19.3) is a single element of the explicitly computed group \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},A(-1)) =\mathbb Z_3^{164}\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)^{59} \oplus(\mathbb Z/9)^{27}\oplus(\mathbb Z/27)^7. \tag{E19.6} \] Its normalized cocycle is determined by the one vector $\eta(\tau)\in A(-1)$, with $\tau$ as in E.18. statement: Fix a rational point or rational tangent on a hyperbolic curve $Y/\mathbb Q$, a coefficient prime $\ell$, and a nilpotency class $c$. The actual continuous coefficient maps are \[ \pi_1(Y_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}) \longrightarrow N^{(\ell)} \longrightarrow N^{(\ell)}/\gamma_{c+1} \longrightarrow U_{\ell,c}(\mathbb Q_\ell), \tag{E22.1} \] where $U_{\ell,c}$ is the class-$c$ unipotent completion. They induce maps of section classes, compatible with every restriction to $G_{\mathbb Q_p}$ and with the point Kummer maps. For a regular model $\mathcal Y/\mathbb Z_S$, $\ell\notin S$, the image of the $S$-integral finite-descent set at $\ell$ is consequently contained in the refined Chabauty--Kim locus for every unipotent quotient. Under the coefficient map $A\to A\otimes\mathbb Q_3$ of E.18, every finite-support obstruction vanishes. Unrestricted support retains the boundedness and convergence test. In particular the finite integral local obstruction modules (E18.4) and (E20.8) map to zero under this specified rationalization. The local point-image conditions used by Chabauty--Kim remain additional conditions on the target cohomology classes, defined by the commuting maps just stated.

statement: Retain the actual cubic notation of E.18--E.19. Put $H=T_3E$, where $E=X_3$, and write $V_{\mathbb Q_3}=H_{\mathbb Q_3}\oplus W_{\mathbb Q_3}$ for its rational compact and boundary summands. Let $w\in\bigwedge^2V$ be the primitive compact determinant vector of E.19, and define the actual submodule and quotient \[ B_w=[V,w]\subset A=\operatorname{Lie}_3(V), \qquad \mathcal Q=A/B_w. \tag{E23.1} \] Then $B_w$ is primitive of rank ten, its bracket map identifies it with $V(1)$ as a $G_{\mathbb Q}$-module, and $\mathcal Q$ is free of rank $320$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)$ and let $\mathcal A=E[3]\rtimes\mu_6$ be the order-$54$ group of $K$-automorphisms of $U=E\setminus E[3]$. Its action on $\mathcal Q$ is independent of base paths. The subspace \[ D=(\mathcal Q_{\mathbb Q_3})^{\mathcal A} \] is $G_{\mathbb Q}$-stable and has the following rational $G_{\mathbb Q}$-module description: \[ D\simeq H_{\mathbb Q_3}(2)\oplus \mathbb Q_3(3)\oplus \mathbb Q_3(3)\varepsilon_K, \tag{E23.2} \] where $\varepsilon_K$ is the quadratic character of $K/\mathbb Q$. In particular $\dim D=4$ and $\operatorname{tr}(c|D)=0$. For $\mathcal G=G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}}$, the image $\overline\eta$ of the actual class of E.19 satisfies \[ \overline\eta\in H^1_{\rm cts}(\mathcal G,D(-1)) \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow H^1_{\rm cts}(\mathcal G,\mathcal Q_{\mathbb Q_3}(-1)), \qquad \dim_{\mathbb Q_3}H^1(\mathcal G,D(-1))=2. \tag{E23.3} \] The two summands with potentially nonzero classes in (E23.2) after twisting by $(-1)$ are $H_{\mathbb Q_3}(1)$ and $\mathbb Q_3(2)\varepsilon_K$; each has one-dimensional unramified global $H^1$. The untwisted quadratic-character summand $\mathbb Q_3(2)$ has zero $H^1$. More explicitly, the original rational class $\eta$ lies in an at-most-eight-dimensional subspace of $H^1(\mathcal G,A_{\mathbb Q_3}(-1))$: it is the inverse image of the two-dimensional subspace in (E23.3) under the map in the exact sequence \[ H^1(\mathcal G,V_{\mathbb Q_3})\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal G,A_{\mathbb Q_3}(-1))\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal G,\mathcal Q_{\mathbb Q_3}(-1)), \qquad \dim H^1(\mathcal G,V_{\mathbb Q_3})=6. \tag{E23.4} \] These are constraints on the actual arithmetic class and the actual quotient maps. They do not evaluate its two projected coordinates, its component in the displayed kernel, or its integral torsion components. No identification of those coordinates with specified polylogarithmic values is asserted.

statement: Let $1\to P\to E\xrightarrow{p}G_K\to1$ be a profinite extension and $t:H_K\to E$ a continuous section over $H_K$. Suppose its $P$-conjugacy class is $Q_K$-invariant. Put \[ C=C_P(t(H_K)),\qquad N=N_E(t(H_K)),\qquad W=N/t(H_K). \] There is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow W\longrightarrow Q_K \longrightarrow1. \tag{F.1} \] Extensions of the actual section $t$ to $G_K$ correspond bijectively to continuous splittings of (F.1); conjugation by $C$ is respected. In particular, $C=1$ gives a unique extension. For a cusp of a hyperbolic curve, a choice of tangential origin identifies $C$ with $T$, and the obstruction is the transgression \[ [o_t]\in H^2_{\rm cts}(Q_K,T),\qquad o_t(q,r)=-c\bigl(u(q)u(r)u(qr)^{-1}\bigr), \tag{F.2} \] where $t(h)=(c(h),h)$ in $T\rtimes G_K$, and $u$ is a continuous set-theoretic transversal for $G_K\to Q_K$. Its vanishing is necessary and sufficient; the extension classes form a torsor under $H^1_{\rm cts}(Q_K,T)$ when nonempty.

statement: Let $L/K$ be finitely generated of characteristic zero, and let $v$ be a valuation of $L$ trivial on $K$. Fix its prolongation to $\overline L$, and write $\Gamma_v=v(L^*)$. There are a split continuous exact sequence and canonical character identifications \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow D_v \longrightarrow G_{\kappa(v)}\longrightarrow1, \qquad I_v=\operatorname{Hom}((\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q)/\Gamma_v, \mu_\infty) =\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T). \] The splitting has no preferred choice, and the action on $I_v$ is cyclotomic. Noncanonically, \[ I_v\simeq\prod_\ell\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^{r_\ell},\qquad r_\ell=\dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}\Gamma_v/\ell\Gamma_v \leq\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}\Gamma_v \leq\operatorname{trdeg}_K L-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(v). \] For $I_v\ne1$, let $\Delta$ be the largest divisible convex subgroup of $\Gamma_v$ and let $w=v/\Delta$ be the coarsening. Then, as actual subgroups for the specified prolongations, \[ I_w=I_v,\qquad N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_w. \] Thus $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ exactly when the residual valuation $v/w$ on $\kappa(w)$ is henselian. In particular it holds for rank one with nonzero inertia. For $I_v=1$ the normalizer is all of $G_L$. These are the precise replacements for the codimension and normalizer assertions on cote 149, scans 119--124 and 127.

statement: Let $K$ be a number field or a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, $V/K$ a smooth geometrically connected variety, and $U/K$ a hyperbolic curve. Call a continuous $G_K$-homomorphism $f:E_V\to E_U$ \emph{point-theoretic} when every point section over a finite extension becomes a point section after a further finite extension. Such an $f$ is either open or kills $P_V$ and is the point section of a unique $K$-rational point composed with $E_V\to G_K$. In particular every such $f$ comes from a unique morphism $V\to U$. For proper $U$ over a number field $K$, condition (F1)(b) holds for every continuous $G_K$-homomorphism $E_V\to E_U$. The all-source assertion (F1) for this proper target and all finite extensions of $K$ is logically equivalent, via composition with point sections, to (F2) for $U$ over those finite extensions. Thus the reduction asked in F(b)(5) is proved for proper targets. For affine targets the point-theoretic hypothesis is the additional premise used in the proved map-level statement.

statement: Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, $V/K$ a smooth geometrically connected variety, $U/K$ a hyperbolic curve, and $f:E_V\to E_U$ a continuous $G_K$-homomorphism. Consequently condition (F1)(b) implies that $H$ is open or trivial. In the trivial case the actual factorization is \[ E_V\longrightarrow G_K\xrightarrow{\,s\,}E_U, \] with $s$ a continuous section. This proves the first assertion of F(b)(5) with the local section theorem explicitly supplied as tool (1) in the prompt~\cite{B_OpenAIPadic}. statement: The cited higher-dimensional theorems yield the following precise parts of F(b)(6). For a sub-$p$-adic field $K$, a normal variety $V/K$, a hyperbolic polycurve $U/K$ of dimension $n$, and an open arithmetic homomorphism $f:E_V\to E_U$, Hoshi's Theorem A gives a unique dominant morphism in each of these ranges: \[ \begin{array}{c|l} n&\text{additional hypotheses}\\ \hline 1&\text{none}\\ 2&\ker f\text{ is topologically finitely generated}\\ 3&\ker f\text{ is finite},\quad V\text{ is of LFG type},\quad\dim V\ge3\\ 4&f\text{ is injective},\quad V\text{ is a hyperbolic polycurve}, \quad\dim V\ge4 . \end{array} \] Here LFG means that every nonconstant morphism from a normal geometric variety to $V_{\overline K}$ has infinite geometric fundamental-group image. In dimension three the resulting map is quasi-finite and $\dim V=3$; in dimension four it is finite \'etale and $\dim V=4$. For $K/\mathbb Q$ finitely generated, Schmidt--Stix, Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6, identify isomorphisms of strongly hyperbolic Artin neighborhoods with outer arithmetic group isomorphisms. The neighborhood hypothesis is a tower of elementary hyperbolic fibrations in which every intermediate variety embeds locally closed into a product of hyperbolic curves. Holzschuh--Schmidt--Stix, in the sharp theorem at the end of their paper, gives dominant relative Hom for $U\to S$ a relative hyperbolic curve, with $S$ normal, connected, excellent and of characteristic zero, and with sub-$p$-adic generic field. The source $V$ is normal and connected, $V\to S$ is flat and of finite type with connected geometric generic fibre, and the smooth locus of $V\to S$ surjects onto $S$. This includes the smooth surjective source in their introductory Theorem A. Its input is a $\pi_1$-open map of profinite \'etale homotopy types over $\mathrm{Et}(S)$, with its commutation homotopy. When $S$ is a hyperbolic polycurve this is exactly the corresponding relative outer-homomorphism datum, through the canonical maps to classifying spaces. Every open arithmetic map between the objects of (F1) satisfies (b). Thus the displayed Hom ranges prove both (a) and (b) for their open maps. The Isom result is the isomorphism range of the same comparison, through the explicit inclusion of isomorphisms among open homomorphisms.

statement: The assertion that an arbitrary open arithmetic map to a hyperbolic polycurve surface must come from a dominant morphism is false already for a smooth proper curve as source. For $C/\mathbb Q$ a smooth proper curve of genus at least two, there is a smooth geometrically connected ample curve $D\subset C\times C$ for which \[ E_D\longrightarrow E_{C\times C} \] is surjective and satisfies (b), although its unique geometric realization is the nondominant inclusion. Its kernel is not topologically finitely generated. For every product $U=U_1\times\cdots\times U_r$ of hyperbolic curves, every open arithmetic map from a normal variety is induced by a unique morphism to $U$, with dominance determined by that morphism's actual image. On arbitrary arithmetic maps, condition (b) is exactly the conjunction of the conditions (b) on all coordinate maps. Consequently universal (F1) for product targets over number fields is equivalent to universal (F2) for curves over number fields, through those coordinate maps.

statement: The comparisons requested in F(a) are given by the following actual forgetful maps, restrictions and identifications. For hyperbolic pairs $(X',S')$, $(X,S)$ over a number field, put $U'=X'\setminus S'$ and $U=X\setminus S$. There is a commutative square \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm dom,\partial}(U',U)&\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow& \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm dom}(U',U)\\ \downarrow\scriptstyle\sim&&\downarrow\scriptstyle\sim\\ \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm open}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B_{U'},\mathcal B_U) &\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow& \operatorname{Hom}^{\rm open}_{G_K}(E_{U'},E_U)/P_U . \end{array} \] The boundary superscript means the literal boundary condition $\overline f^{-1}(S)=S'$ of the corrected 1981 category. The bottom arrow forgets the boundary diagram, its local conjugators and its positive integer degrees. Its image is exactly the inverse image, under the right-hand reconstruction, of that boundary condition. Thus the open curve part of (F1) implies the corrected dominant 1981 assertion; the latter recovers the same (F1) assertion on precisely this displayed image. Every dominant geometric map is represented in the boundary category after the explicitly described shrinkings in the proof. No equivalence obtained by silently forgetting that boundary restriction is asserted. On sections of a geometric curve, the corrected admissibility condition of Longue Marche scan 79 is \[ \text{normalizes no cusp inertia} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C_{P_U}(s(H_K))=1. \] Consequently its assertion that all admissible effective lifts are point sections is equivalent to (F2), and also to the point-source case of (F1), with every cusp packet retained on the (F2) side. The letter's conjecture (7), with its packet correction, is the same point-or-cusp assertion. Its cyclotomic postscript is the right-hand zero-centralizer condition in this displayed comparison. The stronger guess of scan 433 holds for point sections and fails for every cusp section: their $H_K$-fixed subgroups are respectively $1$ and $I_c$. For the full Galois group and all open subgroups its fixed subgroup is $1$ in both cases. Thus the comparison from the full action to its restricted $H_K$-action is literally restriction of the same action, and the exact change of fixed subgroup is as stated. Axioms (1)--(6) of scans 412--421, on realized geometric objects with actual interior points, have the meanings and descent maps proved in B.13. On those objects, replacing ``interior point'' by the intrinsic zero-centralizer selection adds exactly the surjectivity assertion in (F2). For arbitrary abstract outer actions, the inclusion of the geometric objects into that larger collection does not prove essential surjectivity or the intrinsic forms of axioms (5)--(6); those are the unresolved tasks identified in Part B. The first enlargement of the explicitly stated source category in these 1983 assertions is the arbitrary regular finite-type source in scan 48. The relation to the 1981 dimension-at-most-one category is its restriction along $(X,S)\mapsto X\setminus S$. A product of two positive-dimensional hyperbolic curves has dimension two and is permitted as a source in (F1), whereas it is not an object of that stated 1981 category. statement: Let $\mathrm{SC}_{\rm nf}$ denote (F2) over all number fields. There is a proved implication from this assertion to (F2) over finitely generated characteristic-zero fields for every hyperbolic curve $U/K$ admitting a geometric finite \'etale cover $Y\to U_{\overline K}$ and a nonconstant map $Y\to A_{\overline K}$, where $A$ is defined over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. This includes all proper hyperelliptic curves, every hyperbolic type of genus at most two, and every affine curve with such a cover mapping nonconstantly to the tripod. Every curve has a nonempty open subcurve in this last range. This is an implication between the two section assertions, not an assertion that $\mathrm{SC}_{\rm nf}$ has been proved. The general implication asked in F(c), with no cover hypothesis, remains open in this return. The precise next map after spreading already occurs over $K=k(B)$ for a hyperbolic affine curve $B$ over a number field $k$: For a smooth proper hyperbolic family $X\to B$, a generic section gives \[ r:E_B\longrightarrow E_X, \qquad p r=\mathrm{id}, \qquad E_{X_\eta}=E_X\times_{E_B}G_{k(B)}. \] Every such $r$ satisfies (F1)(b) and has non-open image. statement: Fix the rational tangent of parameter $1$ at $0$ on $T=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. Every parameter $t\in\mathbb Q^*$ has the following exact characterization using a specified four-puncture diagram. Put \[ W_t=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,t,\infty\},\qquad p(z)=z,\quad q(z)=z/t, \qquad p,q:W_t\longrightarrow T. \] Repeated punctures at $t=1$ are simply omitted. There is a unique class in the cusp packet at $0$ of $W_t$ whose image under $q_*$ is the parameter-$1$ class; its image under $p_*$ is the parameter-$t$ class of $T$. In packet coordinates the actual maps are \[ p_*:c\longmapsto c,\qquad q_*:c\longmapsto c-\kappa(t). \] In a normalized tripod presentation $P_T=\langle x,y\rangle^{\wedge}$ with the parameter-$1$ section and \[ \rho_\sigma(x)=x^{\chi(\sigma)},\qquad \rho_\sigma(y)=f_\sigma^{-1}y^{\chi(\sigma)}f_\sigma, \qquad f_\sigma\in[P_T,P_T], \] changing that section by a cusp cocycle $c$ gives exactly \[ f^{\,c}_\sigma=f_\sigma x^{-c(\sigma)},\qquad (f^{\,c}_\sigma)^{\rm ab}=(-c(\sigma),0). \] Thus inserting the already specified Kummer cocycle $\kappa(t)$ into these relations recognizes its parameter class. Neither construction removes its input: the first retains the four-puncture diagram with cross-ratio $t$, and the second retains the Kummer character of $t$ and the chosen origin. They do not yet answer the intrinsic single-tripod GT-recognition question left in Proposition~\ref{F-open-tangents}.

statement: Let $U\to B$ be a hyperbolic curve fibration over a hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated characteristic-zero field $K$. Let $c\in(\overline B\setminus B)(K)$. statement: Let $(X,D)$ be a smooth normal-crossings pair over a characteristic-zero field, $U=X\setminus D$, and $S=D_J^*$ a connected open stratum with its $r$ branches labelled. Write $N_j$ for their normal lines on $S$, $P_S=\prod_{j\in J,S}N_j^\times$, and $\mathcal T_S$ for the punctured henselian normal tube. Paths and geometric points are fixed in every displayed fundamental-group map. \begin{enumerate} \item Normal specialization identifies the finite-covering categories of $\mathcal T_S$ and $P_S$. Its profinite geometric homotopy sequence is \[ \pi_2^{\rm et}(S_{\bar K})\xrightarrow{(c_1(N_j))_j} T^J\longrightarrow\pi_1(\mathcal T_{S,\bar K}) \longrightarrow\pi_1(S_{\bar K})\longrightarrow1. \tag{F.43.1} \] The first map means Chern transgression, evaluated on spherical classes. The composite $\iota:T^J\to P_U$ kills its image. Thus injectivity of the full global inertia implies left exactness in (F.43.1). For a relative cusp of a hyperbolic smooth pair, the tube extension maps isomorphically onto the cusp normalizer extension of Proposition~\ref{F-torsors}, with extension class $c_1(N)$. \item At a geometric boundary point, $\iota:T^J\to P_U$ is injective precisely when every finite covering germ is an open and closed sub-germ of the restriction of a finite global covering. If $R_{\bf n}$ is the finite root stack with orders $n_i$, and $M_{\bf n}$ is the closed normal subgroup of $P_U$ generated by the $n_i$th powers of boundary inertia, then \[ \pi_1(R_{{\bf n},\bar K})=P_U/M_{\bf n},\qquad \ker(T^J\to\pi_1(R_{{\bf n},\bar K})) =\iota^{-1}(M_{\bf n}),\qquad \bigcap_{\bf n}\iota^{-1}(M_{\bf n})=\ker\iota. \tag{F.43.2} \] In particular a finite root stack can enlarge this kernel. \item Horizontal cusp inertia injects in a tower of punctured hyperbolic smooth pairs. In the recursively compatible stable toroidal range of LM5 F.39, the full crossing inertia injects as well. The hypothesis here retains the stable incidence data: the kernel of the local contact matrix is the fibre puncture or the essential vanishing cycle. On split branches the Galois action is cyclotomic; in general it also permutes the factors. A monomial map $z'_j=u_j\prod_i z_i^{m_{ji}}$ induces the matrix $(m_{ji})$ on these inertia groups. \item For $y^2=x^3+t$, the model \[ [\{Y^2=X^3+1\}\times\mathbb A^1_s/\mu_6],\qquad \zeta(X,Y,s)=(\zeta^{-2}X,\zeta^{-3}Y,\zeta s), \tag{F.43.3} \] has open part identified with the original family by $t=s^6$, $x=s^2X$, $y=s^3Y$. Its normal meridian injects; the full corner meridian does too when the infinity section is retained. On the ordinary embedded cusp resolution the two exceptional-tail crossing maps instead have respective kernels $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(-3,1)$ and $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(-2,1)$. These are maps into the same open fundamental group, with the explicit substitutions above and in the proof. \item The maps in (F.43.1), restricted to a relative cusp or a trait meeting that cusp, are exactly the maps in FLAGGED\_149 C3, C4, C6, C8, and C9. C1, C2, and C5 give the corresponding extension tests for an \emph{already given rational geometric section}. Their geometric premise is retained; the tests do not construct a geometric point from an arbitrary section. \end{enumerate} This supplies the added comparison of LM5 F.21--F.23, F.35, F.39 with FLAGGED\_149 C1--C6, C8, C9.

statement: Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated and let $U\to B$ be a hyperbolic curve fibration over a hyperbolic curve. Let $s:G_K\to E_U$ project to a cuspidal section $\tau$ at $c\in(\overline B\setminus B)(K)$. Suppose the fibre over $K((t))$, for a parameter $t$ at $c$, has potentially good marked reduction. Let $Y_\tau/K$ be the smooth residue curve obtained by the descent construction of Proposition~\ref{F-reduction}; it has an identified arithmetic extension \[ E_{Y_\tau}\simeq E_{U_{K((t))}}\mathbin{\times}_{G_{K((t))},\tau}G_K. \tag{F.44.1} \] Every $s$ whose induced section in (F.44.1) is a point or cusp section has a birational lift $G_K\to G_{K(U)}$. The lift can be obtained through the decomposition group of a rank-two valuation of $K((t))(U)$ with residue $K$. Consequently universal curve lifting implies surface lifting for hyperbolic fibrations with potentially good marked reduction at every rational base cusp after finite constant extension. This extends the good-reduction range of Proposition~\ref{F-good-boundary-lifting}; the implication is an implication between the two universal assertions, not an assertion of universal curve lifting.

statement: Let $K$ be a number field, $U=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, $E=\pi_1(U)$, and $\Delta=\ker(E\to G_K)$. Fix an actual lifted cusp inertia $I_0\subset\Delta$ above $0$ and a continuous section $s:G_K\to N_E(I_0)$. Its class is induced by a nonzero $K$-rational tangent vector at $0$ precisely when the following entirely group-theoretic relation holds. There exist an open subgroup $H\subset E$ with image $G_K$, a cusp inertia $J$ of $H$, a continuous section $\sigma:G_K\to N_H(J)$ of the arithmetic projection, and two continuous open homomorphisms over $G_K$, \[ p,q:H\longrightarrow E, \] such that \[ \begin{gathered} p|_J:J\xrightarrow{\sim} I_0,\qquad q(j)=p(j)^2\quad(j\in J),\\ [p\circ\sigma]=[q\circ\sigma]=[s] \quad\text{modulo conjugation by }\Delta. \tag{F.45.1} \end{gathered} \] Here a cusp inertia of $H$ is an intersection $H\cap aI_i a^{-1}$ for one of the three ambient peripheral classes and an actual geometric conjugator $a$. The peripheral classes themselves are characterized by the cyclotomic-normalizer criterion. Thus all the quantifiers in (F.45.1) refer to the one ambient arithmetic group, its open subgroups, their continuous homomorphisms, and their sections; the test does not first declare any source section geometric. The same relation after restriction to some finite extension $L/K$ is equivalent to (F.45.1) over $K$. For every specified $t\in K^\times$, one can moreover choose $H,J,p,q$ so that the common-image relation in (F.45.1), with $\sigma$ in that cusp packet, has the unique image $[s_t]$, the tangent with coordinate $t$ in the standard coordinate $z$ at $0$. This supplies a uniform global relation recognizing the geometric splittings in F(g)(5), using two open Hom maps. It does not replace those maps by a word involving only the automorphisms of the tripod or only the two entries of a Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller pair. That more restrictive formula remains the separate question in Proposition~\ref{F-open-tangents}.

statement: In Theorem~\ref{F-two-Hom-tangents} over $K=\mathbb Q$, impose the additional requirement that both $p$ and $q$ be injective. The resulting relation holds exactly for \[ [s_{16}],\quad [s_{-16}]. \tag{F.46.1} \] More generally, over a number field $K$, every tangent parameter selected by this restricted relation belongs to $16\mu(K)$, where $\mu(K)$ is the group of roots of unity in $K$. This conclusion still holds when the local degrees one and two in that relation are replaced by any two unequal positive degrees $d,e$: require that $p$ and $q$ send the selected cusp inertia into $I_0$ with these respective indices, and keep the common-image equation for the section. Every common image is then an ordinary tangent in $16\mu(K)$. In particular, over $\mathbb Q$ even the union of all these unequal-degree finite-\'etale tests selects exactly the two classes in (F.46.1). The condition $d\ne e$ is essential: taking $p=q$ gives an equal-degree relation satisfied by every member of the corresponding packet. The additional requirement is exactly that the two reconstructed morphisms from the common finite cover to the tripod are finite \'etale. In that case $q\circ p^{-1}:p(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}q(H)$ is an actual isomorphism between open arithmetic subgroups. Thus the forgetful map from these finite-cover relations to the open-Hom relations of Theorem~\ref{F-two-Hom-tangents} has a strictly smaller set of common section images: $[s_2]$ is an explicit witness. This refutes replacing the two maps in that criterion by such commensurations while retaining its inertia degrees and equal-image equation. It makes no assertion that every different formula using only GT automorphisms has this same restriction.

statement: Put $K=\mathbb Q(i)$, $\Gamma=G_K$, $\Gamma^\circ=G_{K(\mu_\infty)}$, and $U=\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. There is an abstract semilinear $\Gamma$-action on the geometric universal covering $\mathcal U$ of this same tripod for which the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item Its restriction to every open subgroup of $\Gamma^\circ$ is not functionwise continuous. Its action on the finite geometric homology quotient $H_1(U_{\overline K},\mathbb F_3)$ is already discontinuous. \item No open subgroup of $\Gamma^\circ$ admits a finite-type quotient $\mathcal U\to W$ which is a connected pro-\'etale covering and on which the induced semilinear action is functionwise continuous. In particular, no open subgroup of $\Gamma$ admits such a quotient. \item The completed universal covering nevertheless has exactly one fixed pro-point under this abstract $\Gamma^\circ$-action, namely the chosen lift of $1/2$. It is also fixed by the whole abstract $\Gamma$-action. \end{enumerate} Thus the inclusion of continuous actions into abstract actions is strict already on the actual cyclotomic-kernel domain occurring in (B$'$). The continuous finite-form descent of Proposition~\ref{F-continuous-action} does not extend to these actions. The universal fixed-point existence assertion for arbitrary abstract actions is neither proved nor refuted by this example.
